pick_list.notes: Use stainless or zinc-plated alloy steel after corrosion/strength decision. Button-head is preferred where carriage clearance matters.

pick_list.source_basis: CAD/BOM_README.md M5 fastener totals: 2 per Z bottom bearing holder
pick_list.notes: Z bottom bearing holder (bom/data.json id 91) into drop-in T-nuts in the C-beam channel-floor slots; heads sit in the holder's counterbores.

Confirm connector plate geometry for each of the 27 C-beam joints before buying all plates in one style.

Z hardware re-derived for the lead-screw CAD (BOM v2.9.0, 2026-10-12) by CAD/bom_generate.py: the belt-Z bottom idlers (4 M5 x 30 axles, 4 nyloc, 8 washers) and the top-plate screws/T-nuts are gone; Z motor screws are M5 x 16 into the motor mount's nut traps (the 28 M5 nuts above still cover all 7 motors); each Z nut block adds 2 M5 x 16; each Z bottom holder adds 2 M5 x 20 + 2 drop-in T-nuts. Couplers and lock collars use their own set screws, the 608ZZ is a press fit, and the motor-mount tab is clamped by the existing post-to-top-rail joint screws.

Verify at assembly: the Y-gantry rail end sits about 1 mm off the Z carriage plate's outer face over both nut-block holes at every post, so the nut-block bolts cannot take nuts there. Thread them into the plate from the channel side (tap M5 in a plate thick enough, or use heat-set inserts in a printed plate); a 3 mm plate is too thin to tap reliably.
Verify that drop-in T-nuts fit the C-beam channel-floor slots used by the Z bottom holders.
